threads.body: [General] Removing the post-`@` check makes `hasMultipleTargets()` return false for `jdbc:mariadb:failover://alice:p;ss@h1,unexpected=value/db`, because it stops at `;` while `extractAuthority()` does not. The group parser rejects the second endpoint, but single-server fallback remains enabled and reports the username `alice` as the configured server. Count targets using the same authority boundaries as group parsing for URL-shaped schemes, retain semicolon-property boundaries for schemes that require them, and add a regression test for this rejected-group case.

@copilot Update this PR directly to fix the authority-boundary mismatch identified in Copilot review 5731736383, comment 4438611970. Keep the original goal: simple grammar-aligned parsing without malformed-password guessing.

At head 4d985cb1c31fa97250662b4e4e5d60c8a7df1b00, UrlParsingUtils.extractAuthority ends at '/', '?', or '#', but hasMultipleTargets also stops at ';' for every scheme. JdbcConnectionUrlParser uses the latter to disable single-server fallback, and MysqlUrlParser.applyHostGroup also uses it after group parsing rejects an entry.

For example, consider jdbc:mariadb:failover://alice:p;ss@h1,unexpected=value/db. The semicolon is within userinfo for this URL-shaped grammar, not a connection-property boundary. hasMultipleTargets sees only alice:p and returns false. Group extraction sees both hosts and rejects unexpected=value, but fallback remains enabled. parseMariaSubProtocol then treats alice as the host and reports it as the configured server instead of dropping the rejected group.

Align target counting with the authority grammar used by the parser. Preserve real semicolon-property boundaries for SQL Server, jTDS, Derby, and any other applicable drivers, without introducing new guesses about credentials after path/query/fragment boundaries. Ensure a rejected multi-host list cannot fall back to a partial or credential-derived singleton. Add a focused regression for this MariaDB semicolon-userinfo/rejected-group case and retain the existing semicolon-property and late-at-sign regression coverage. Make the smallest complete fix and run the narrow formatter and relevant JDBC parser tests. Do not modify unrelated PRs or create a new PR.

[General] HSQLDB's network schemes are missing here, so `jdbc:hsqldb:http://hs.host;password=a,b` is incorrectly counted as multiple targets. This disables single-server fallback and drops the configured `hs.host` target, even though `HsqlUrlParser` handles these semicolon-delimited properties through `ParseContext.parseUrl()`. Include `hsqldb:` schemes and add a regression for a pathless URL with a comma-containing property.

replies.body: Fixed in 6615b5f8145e. All four HSQLDB network modes now retain their semicolon-property boundaries when counting targets. Added pathless-URL regressions with comma-containing properties and covered the other semicolon-aware parser paths.

@copilot Update this PR directly to require an explicit authority-grammar decision from every JDBC URL parser, without changing supported runtime parsing behavior.

In instrumentation/jdbc/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jdbc/internal/parser/JdbcUrlParser.java, remove the default implementation of extractAuthority and declare it as an abstract nullable method. Update every implementing parser to make its authority extraction choice explicitly. Reuse UrlParsingUtils.extractAuthority for URL-shaped grammar and extractSemicolonAuthority for semicolon-property grammar as appropriate. Preserve parser-specific decisions, including OceanBase's subtype-dependent handling. Return null only where authority extraction is genuinely inapplicable to the supported URL forms. Do not introduce a new parser hierarchy or abstraction just to avoid small explicit overrides.

The purpose is to prevent a future parser from silently inheriting the wrong grammar. Neither delimiter policy is universally safe when extracted text is converted into telemetry: semicolon-property text may contain credentials, while a semicolon in URL userinfo must not truncate credentials before their terminating at sign. This is a defensive API cleanup, not a request to change accepted grammars or claim that the current default itself leaks credentials. The interface method currently participates in multi-target/fallback detection, and MySQL/MariaDB parse their actual host lists independently.

Preserve the unknown-driver semicolon bailout in JdbcConnectionUrlParser, separately supplied DataSource properties, ordinary userinfo stripping, semicolon-property dialects, MariaDB semicolon-containing userinfo, rejected multi-host fallback protection, and late-at-sign path/query behavior. Keep the existing utility-level fallback for an unknown parser. Do not restore malformed-password guessing or fix unrelated parsing issues.

Ensure every implementation compiles with the now-required method, retain the focused authority-boundary/privacy regressions, and add narrowly targeted coverage only where needed for the explicit choices. Run the narrow relevant spotlessApply task directly before the relevant JDBC parser tests. Update this existing PR rather than creating another PR. Do not modify unrelated work.

@copilot Update this PR directly to make authority handling and configured-target fallback safety part of parsing, not a separate operation on the parser interface. This supersedes the earlier explicit-extractAuthority-interface cleanup.

At head f8a5cfe47d1ac22052404f24b233201020edd8d6, JdbcConnectionUrlParser first calls parser.extractAuthority, detects multiple targets, and disables single-server fallback before calling parser.parse. The dispatcher even needs a MySQL exception. This splits grammar ownership: the preliminary authority pass and actual parsing must agree about boundaries.

Leave only void parse(String jdbcUrl, ParseContext ctx) on JdbcUrlParser. Remove extractAuthority from that interface and remove the per-parser overrides that exist solely for the dispatcher. Remove the dispatcher's authority extraction, multi-target prepass, and associated unused imports. Each parser or its existing shared parsing helper must instead detect multiple targets and resolve or suppress singleton fallback as part of its normal parsing path, using the same grammar boundaries as the parsing itself. Authority-extraction utility helpers can remain internally where useful; do not replace the interface method with another externally coordinated parsing phase.

Possible reuse points, not a required patch recipe: ParseContext.parseUrl already splits semicolon-delimited properties before parsing the host, so that path can detect multiple targets from its existing URL portion. GenericUrlParser.applyHostGroup already resolves a configured group or disables fallback for a rejected group. MySQL/MariaDB already parse and resolve their actual host lists independently. Inspect every registered parser, including custom paths that do not use those helpers, before removing the dispatcher safeguard. Keep necessary safety logic before any partial host result can escape through best-effort exception handling. Reuse shared grammar-aware logic where appropriate without introducing a new parser hierarchy, duplicated prepasses, or an unnecessary abstraction.

Preserve supported parsing behavior and existing credential/privacy safeguards: a rejected multi-host list must not fall back to a partial or credential-derived singleton; semicolon-property commas must not affect host counting; semicolons inside URL userinfo must not truncate it. Preserve OceanBase subtype-specific grammar, all existing semicolon dialects, MySQL/MariaDB host parsing, default-port behavior, DataSource property precedence, and late-at-sign path/query behavior. Keep the unknown-driver semicolon bailout and separately supplied DataSource properties in JdbcConnectionUrlParser. Do not restore malformed-password guessing or fix unrelated parsing issues.

Update tests that currently call the removed parser-interface method to cover the behavior through parsing and observable DbInfo/configured-target results where appropriate. Retain the existing focused privacy, boundary, rejected-group, and unknown-driver regressions, and add narrowly targeted coverage for any safety logic relocated out of the dispatcher. Update this existing PR rather than creating another PR, and do not modify unrelated work.
